finding.claim: purge handler performs the destructive purgeAll() operation without enforcing the admin permission; the checkPerm result is discarded, so any user regardless of permissions can trigger it.
finding.source: Any HTTP request reaching the purge handler with a *User in request context (handlers.go:25); the user's Perms may contain no 'admin' entry. Route registration and auth middleware are not in this directory.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from context
checkPerm(u, "admin") evaluated but its boolean return is discarded
checkPerm returns u.Perms[perm]; no side effects, cannot stop the request
purgeAll() runs unconditionally (stub at line 44; real impact unknown)

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm is called but its result is ignored, so it is not a control. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22), which returns 403 on failure, is not called in purge; rotateKeys (handlers.go:33) uses it correctly. No early return follows the check. No auth middleware, HTTP method restriction, or CSRF protection is present in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. checkPerm at handlers.go:26 is a bare statement whose bool return is discarded (checkPerm is defined at handlers.go:12-14 with no side effects). mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22, returns 403) is not called in purge, though rotateKeys uses it at handlers.go:33. No early return follows the check before purgeAll() at handlers.go:27. Route registration and auth middleware are not in this directory, so any route-level gating is unknown.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the source: the check at handlers.go:26 is a discarded bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any request that reaches purge with a *User in context. The residual uncertainty is whether routing restricts this handler to admins, which this directory cannot show, but the handler itself enforces no admin check, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33.

finding.claim: userFrom uses an unchecked type assertion, so a request with no userKey{} value in context panics instead of being rejected with 401. This is a request-level crash, not an authorization bypass, because the panic occurs before purgeAll or rotateAll runs.
finding.source: A request reaching purge or rotateKeys without a userKey{} value in context, e.g. if auth middleware is absent or skipped on that route.

trace.note: bare .(*User) assertion panics when the context value is absent; net/http recovers per request

finding.guards_checked: No nil or ok-form check on the assertion. The panic happens before any side effect in purge (line 27) or rotateKeys (line 36), so it does not allow the protected operation to run.

verdict.guard_found: none. handlers.go:40 is a bare `.(*User)` assertion with no ok-form or nil check. The only other checks are checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) and mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22), which run after userFrom and cannot prevent the panic.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: userFrom at handlers.go:40 panics when the context lacks userKey{}, and purge (handlers.go:25) and rotateKeys (handlers.go:32) both call it before any side effect, so the narrow crash claim holds. Reachability depends on routing that is not in this directory, since no route registration or middleware appears in the code, so the source is conditional. Separately, handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's bool, so purge runs for any authenticated user; that is a real authorization bug the candidate does not describe.
